item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, a lake that is clear, bright, not stirred up. A person with good eyes standing on the bank can see the oysters,…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, a lake that is clear, bright, not stirred up. A person with good eyes standing on the bank can see the oysters, the shells, the gravel, the pebbles, the schools of fish moving about and resting. Why is that? Because the water is not stirred up, bhikkhus. So too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu with a mind not stirred up can know his own benefit, can know the benefit of others, can know the benefit of both, can realize a superior human state, the truly noble distinction of knowledge and vision — this is possible. Why is that? Because the mind is not stirred up, bhikkhus.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.46

item.title: Cunda, that a person who is himself sunk in mud could pull out another sunk in mud — this is impossible. Cunda, that a person…
item.description:
Cunda, that a person who is himself sunk in mud could pull out another sunk in mud — this is impossible. Cunda, that a person who is not sunk in mud could pull out another sunk in mud — this is possible. Cunda, that a person who is not tamed, not trained, not fully liberated, could tame, train, and fully liberate another — this is impossible. That a person who is tamed, trained, fully liberated, could tame, train, and fully liberate another — this is possible.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 8 – Sallekhasutta

item.title: Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, in the presence of the Blessed One, spoke these appropriate verses in praise: 'Today is the pure fifteenth, Five hundred bhikkhus…
item.description:
Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, in the presence of the Blessed One, spoke these appropriate verses in praise:

'Today is the pure fifteenth,
Five hundred bhikkhus have gathered,
The noble ones have cut the fetters,
Without afflictions, ended rebirth.

Like a Wheel-turning Monarch,
With ministers attending him,
Travels all the four directions,
From this land to the ocean's edge.

So too, the disciples,
Who have attained the three knowledges,
Have slain death,
These ones attend upon
The victor in battle,
The supreme caravan leader.

All are sons of the Blessed One,
None is useless.
I reverently pay homage
To the one who has pulled out the dart of craving,
I respectfully honor
The one of the sun's lineage.'

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 8.7

item.title: Possessing these four qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in hell. What four? Possessing evil bodily action, evil verbal action, evil mental action, and being…
item.description:
Possessing these four qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in hell. What four? Possessing evil bodily action, evil verbal action, evil mental action, and being ungrateful, unthankful. Possessing these four qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in hell.
Possessing these four qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in heaven. What four? Possessing good bodily action, good verbal action, good mental action, and being grateful, thankful. Possessing these four qualities, bhikkhus, as such is placed in heaven.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.213

item.title: One who is skilled in the goal, One who knows the peaceful path, Should act like this: After understanding clearly, Being capable, upright, Truly, well…
item.description:
One who is skilled in the goal,
One who knows the peaceful path,
Should act like this:
After understanding clearly,
Being capable, upright,
Truly, well direct, easy to speak to,
Gentle, without conceit.

Content, easily supported,
With few duties, living simply,
With peaceful faculties, wise,
Not arrogant, without greed for families.

One should not commit any trivial fault
That other wise people might criticize.
May all beings be happy and secure,
May they attain happiness and well-being.

Whatever living beings there are,
Frail or strong, without exception,
Long or large, medium or short,
Subtle or gross, seen or unseen,
Those living far or near,
Those already born or seeking birth,
May all beings be happy and well.

From: Khuddakapāṭha 9

item.title: Māluṅkyaputta, just as a man shot with a dart thickly smeared with poison. His friends and relatives summon a surgeon. But the man says: 'I…
item.description:
Māluṅkyaputta, just as a man shot with a dart thickly smeared with poison. His friends and relatives summon a surgeon. But the man says: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know whether the man who shot me was a noble, a brahmin, a merchant, or a worker.' He might say: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know the name and clan of the man who shot me.' He might say: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know whether the man who shot me was tall, short, or of medium height.' He might say: 'I will not have this dart removed until I know whether the man who shot me was dark, tawny, or golden.' ... Māluṅkyaputta, that man would die and still not know these things. So too, Māluṅkyaputta, whoever says: 'I will not live the holy life under the Blessed One until he answers me: "The world is eternal" or "the world is not eternal" ... "the Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death" — that person will die and still not have had these things answered by the Tathāgata. Māluṅkyaputta, the holy life does not depend on the view that the world is eternal. The holy life does not depend on the view that the world is not eternal. Whether there is the view that the world is eternal or the view that the world is not eternal, there is still birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, and I teach their abandonment here and now.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 63 – Cūḷamālukyasutta

item.title: Just as, bhikkhus, a tree with its branches and leaves destroyed: then its shoots do not reach completeness, its bark does not reach completeness, its…
item.description:
Just as, bhikkhus, a tree with its branches and leaves destroyed: then its shoots do not reach completeness, its bark does not reach completeness, its sapwood does not reach completeness, its heartwood does not reach completeness. So too, bhikkhus, for an immoral person, one of broken virtue, right concentration is thereby destroyed. When right concentration is absent, for one whose right concentration is destroyed, true knowledge and vision of things as they really are is thereby destroyed. When true knowledge and vision is absent, for one whose true knowledge and vision is destroyed, disenchantment and dispassion are thereby destroyed. When disenchantment and dispassion are absent, for one whose disenchantment and dispassion are destroyed, the knowledge and vision of liberation is thereby destroyed.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.24

item.title: He drenches, saturates, fills, and suffuses his body with the rapture and ease born of concentration, so that no part of his entire body is…
item.description:
He drenches, saturates, fills, and suffuses his body with the rapture and ease born of concentration, so that no part of his entire body is not suffused with that rapture and ease born of concentration. Great king, this is a visible fruit of the ascetic life, more excellent and sublime than previous visible fruits of the ascetic life.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 2 – Sāmaññaphalasutta

item.title: Here, Udāyi, a person lives dedicated to the abandoning of bases, to the relinquishment of bases. But while he lives dedicated to the abandoning of…
item.description:
Here, Udāyi, a person lives dedicated to the abandoning of bases, to the relinquishment of bases. But while he lives dedicated to the abandoning of bases, to the relinquishment of bases, thoughts and reflections connected with bases arise. He tolerates them, does not abandon them, does not relinquish them, does not terminate them, does not destroy them. Udāyi, I say: 'That person is bound, not unbound.' Why is that? Because the difference in his faculties is clearly known to me.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 66 – Laṭukikopamasutta

item.title: On the slopes of the Snowy Mountain lives a tribe of upright people, With abundant wealth and energy, in the Kosala land. Born in the…
item.description:
On the slopes of the Snowy Mountain lives a tribe of upright people,
With abundant wealth and energy, in the Kosala land.

Born in the solar clan, the Sakya family,
Leaving that family, I went forth, O king.
I have no longing for sensual pleasures.

Seeing the danger in sensual pleasures, abandoning them is security.
I will go, striving; my mind is joyful.

From: Sutta Nipāta 3.1
